speaker: amari_ndlovu
headline: DELIVERY LANDS IN A CULTURAL LANDSCAPE.
deck: The same policy arrives differently when language, memory, local authority and historical experience shape how people interpret the state.
quote: Institutions enter communities that already have memory, meaning and ways of recognising one another.
facts: Place gives policy a lived setting rather than an abstract target.
Language determines whether information becomes usable knowledge.
Memory shapes trust long before a new programme begins.
Dignity depends on whether public action recognises people as participants, not recipients.
takeaway: Public legitimacy grows when delivery enters the cultural landscape with recognition rather than erasure.
